title: Cardinality budget + labeling proposal (tier/model/route SLOs)
content:
Context / why this doc exists

The “Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy” initiative depends on breaking down success/latency indicators by tier (Hosted vs Dedicated), region, model, and route/endpoint. The straightforward approach (“just add labels for everything”) will push us into a bad place:

- Active-series explosion (storage + ingest)
- Slow / expensive queries (especially ad-hoc dashboards)
- High alerting load (flappy burn-rate alerts due to sparse series)
- Increased risk of mis-attribution (especially for streaming disconnects)

This proposal sets:
1) A labeling standard for tier/model/route views that SRE + Platform + Product actually need.
2) A cardinality budget and enforcement plan so we can ship tiered SLOs without blowing up cost or operability.

This is written primarily for Gateway, Routing, Runtime instrumentation owners and the Telemetry platform.

Scope

In-scope
- Metrics emitted from gateway → routing → runtime that power:
  - Availability / error-rate SLI
  - Timeouts SLI
  - Streaming disconnect SLI
  - Latency SLIs (TTFT + non-streaming p95/p99)
  - Dedicated pool readiness SLI (special-case)
- Dimensions required to implement tier-aware SLOs and error budgets (dashboards + alert rules + gating checks).

Out of scope
- Full trace/log schema (we can use logs for high-card debug; see “escape hatches”).
- Customer-facing, per-customer reliability dashboards (Dedicated): we will support this via controlled aggregation and separate “restricted views”; not by putting customer_id on core SLI metrics.

Non-goals
- “Perfect” per-model/per-route/per-customer everything in Prometheus. We want: reliable SLO math + usable dashboards + controlled costs.


Quick summary of recommendations

A. Adopt a 3-tier metrics model (“Gold / Silver / Debug”)
- Gold: SLO + burn-rate alerting + gating. Very limited label set. Long retention.
- Silver: Engineering dashboards. Moderate label set. Medium retention.
- Debug: High-cardinality, sampled, short retention OR logs only.

B. Standardize the canonical label vocabulary (and disallow everything else on SLI metrics)
Required labels for Gold SLI metrics:
- tier (hosted|dedicated)
- region (e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1)
- endpoint_family (chat|completions|embeddings|rerank|catalog)
- stream (true|false) — only for endpoint families where it applies

Allowed labels for Silver (additional):
- route (canonical route id, NOT raw URL path)
- model (canonical model id, bounded set)
- model_family (optional rollup, e.g., llama3, qwen2)
- status_class (2xx|4xx|5xx|timeout|disconnect) (bounded)

Disallowed on Gold/Silver SLI metrics:
- customer_id / org_id / api_key_id
- raw_path
- request_id / trace_id
- prompt_hash
- user_agent
- pod_id / instance_id (unless explicitly part of an infra metric)

C. Enforce series budgets per metric family and per service
- We will establish a per-service “active series budget” for SLI metrics and a hard fail in CI for new metrics violating the budget (phased: warn-only → block).

D. Default to aggregation for “route” and “model”
- route: use a bounded route vocabulary (route IDs) and/or route groups.
- model: use a bounded list of “SLO models” (Redwood-supported + top-N), with an “other” bucket.


Background: where cardinality explodes for us

We tend to add labels that individually look reasonable but become combinatorially large:
- region (6–10)
- tier (2)
- route/raw path (50–200+; raw paths can be unbounded)
- model (20–80+ variants, grows quickly)
- status_code (20–60)
- customer/org (Hosted: thousands; Dedicated: hundreds)
- streaming flags + disconnect reasons (5–15)

Even if each dimension seems small, “route x model x region x status_code x tier” quickly gets into tens/hundreds of thousands of series per metric.

SLO math itself (error budgets) is sensitive to sparse series:
- If a label produces low volume per time window, the calculated burn-rate becomes noisy.
- SRE ends up turning off alerting or adding complicated query guards.


Cardinality budgets (proposed)

We need budgets that are understandable and enforceable.

Definitions
- Active series: unique time series currently being ingested (Prometheus notion).
- SLI metric families: the “golden” counters/histograms we’ll use for SLO computation.

Budget targets (initial)
- Per service (gateway / routing / runtime / control plane):
  - Gold SLI metrics combined: <= 25k active series per region
  - Silver SLI metrics combined: <= 75k active series per region
  - Debug metrics: no fixed budget; must be (a) sampled and (b) <= 7 days retention OR moved to logs.

Rationale
- We’re optimizing for predictable query costs and reliable alert behavior.
- These numbers are chosen as “tight enough to force discipline” but leave room for region expansion.

Enforcement stages
- Phase 0 (now): publish label rules + add dashboards showing active-series by service/metric
- Phase 1: CI “warn-only” check for new/changed metrics label sets
- Phase 2: block merges that introduce prohibited labels on SLI metrics
- Phase 3: block merges that exceed active-series budgets for Gold/Silver families

Owner proposal
- Telemetry platform: Logan Wright / Caleb Johnson (implementation + dashboards)
- SLO program: Aisha Bello (requirements sign-off)
- Each service team (gateway/routing/runtime): metric owner for compliance


Canonical labeling standard

This section is the “source of truth” for what labels mean and how to populate them. The intent is that gateway, routing, and runtime all converge on the same values so cross-service SLI computation doesn’t require per-service translation.

Global conventions
- Labels must be low-card and explicitly enumerated.
- Values must be stable over time (avoid “v2” style churn, avoid embedding version numbers unless the set is bounded).
- Prefer rollups to “raw values.”

Label definitions

1) tier (required; Gold/Silver)
- hosted: Redwood API multi-tenant
- dedicated: Dedicated pools

Population rule
- Set once at ingress (gateway) based on tenant configuration; propagate through request context.
- Must not be inferred by downstream services.

2) region (required; Gold/Silver)
- Cloud region where the request was served.

Population rule
- Use Redwood region identifiers used by routing policy (must match Console filters).

3) endpoint_family (required; Gold/Silver)
Proposed enum:
- chat
- completions
- embeddings
- rerank
- catalog

Notes
- “catalog” includes model list/metadata operations that affect “model catalog operations” SLO.

4) stream (required for chat/completions; Gold/Silver)
- true|false

Notes
- This is used to split TTFT vs non-streaming latency and to separate streaming disconnect SLI.

5) route (Silver only)
- Canonical route id. Must be bounded.

Population rule
- route is derived from the gateway route template or an explicit route_id mapping.
- Never use raw_path.

Examples
- v1_chat_completions
- v1_completions
- v1_embeddings
- v1_rerank
- v1_models_list

(If we need to split more granularly, we add “route_group” first, not new routes everywhere.)

6) model (Silver only)
- Canonical model id (bounded set).

Population rules
- For Gold metrics: do not include model.
- For Silver: include model only if the value is in the allowlist for that tier.
- Otherwise, set model="other".

Proposed allowlist strategy (per tier)
- hosted: top-N (by volume) + any “Redwood curated” flagship models
- dedicated: models explicitly pinned by Dedicated customers (still likely bounded) but do not include customer label

7) model_family (optional; Silver)
- Rollup family (e.g., llama3, qwen2, mistral)

Notes
- model_family is preferred for most dashboards; model is for deeper dives.

8) status_class (Silver only)
Proposed enum (bounded):
- success
- client_error
- server_error
- timeout
- disconnect

Notes
- We should avoid labeling by raw HTTP status_code on SLI metrics. If needed for debugging, do it in Debug metrics or logs.

9) disconnect_reason (Debug only)
Proposed values (bounded but still higher):
- client_abort
- server_disconnect
- upstream_reset
- idle_timeout
- unknown

Notes
- This is valuable but not required for SLO compliance. Use Debug only (sampled) to avoid high series counts.


Metric families (proposed) and label sets

We should keep the number of distinct metric names small and re-use the same label sets.

Gold (SLO computation + burn alerts)

A) redwood_requests_total
Type: counter
Meaning: Count of requests admitted to the system (after auth) with outcome classification.
Labels:
- tier
- region
- endpoint_family
- stream
- outcome (success|failure)

Notes
- Outcome is the simplest possible split to support success-rate SLI.
- We intentionally do NOT break down by route/model here.

B) redwood_request_failures_total
Type: counter
Meaning: Count of failures by broad failure class.
Labels:
- tier
- region
- endpoint_family
- stream
- failure_class (server_error|timeout|disconnect)

Notes
- Keep failure_class small. 4xx are excluded from SLO by definition; they should be tracked separately in non-SLI metrics.

C) redwood_latency_seconds_bucket
Type: histogram
Meaning: End-to-end latency for requests.
Labels:
- tier
- region
- endpoint_family
- stream
- latency_mode (e2e|ttft)

Notes
- For non-streaming endpoints: latency_mode=e2e only.
- For streaming endpoints: emit both ttft and e2e only if we can do it without doubling cost too much. If too expensive, keep Gold=ttft only and move e2e stream duration to Silver.

Silver (dashboards; controlled cost)

D) redwood_requests_total_silver
Type: counter
Labels:
- tier
- region
- endpoint_family
- stream
- route
- model_family
- model
- status_class

Notes
- This is the workhorse for “tier/model/route breakdown” in Console and internal dashboards.
- It is explicitly not used for alerting.

E) redwood_latency_seconds_bucket_silver
Type: histogram
Labels:
- tier
- region
- endpoint_family
- stream
- route
- model_family
- model
- latency_mode (e2e|ttft)

Debug (sampled and/or short retention)

F) redwood_disconnects_total_debug
Type: counter
Labels:
- tier
- region
- endpoint_family
- stream
- route
- disconnect_reason


Dedicated pool readiness (special case)

Dedicated readiness has different properties: the “entity” is a pool, not a request.

G) redwood_dedicated_pool_ready
Type: gauge
Meaning: 1 if pool is considered ready to serve, else 0.
Labels:
- region
- pool_id (bounded; Dedicated pools are limited)

Constraints
- pool_id cardinality is acceptable because Dedicated pool count is bounded (order of hundreds) and not per-request.
- Do NOT join this with per-request metrics by adding pool_id to request metrics.


Controls to keep labels bounded

1) Route normalization
We must ensure “route” is not accidentally unbounded.

Rules
- “route” must be an enum defined in the gateway routing table or a shared config package.
- Block any metric emitter that sets route from request.path directly.

Implementation note
- Add a gateway library helper: canonical_route_id(req) returning the stable route.

2) Model allowlisting and “other” bucketing
We need model breakdowns, but not at infinite scale.

Rules
- Emit model label only via a function that maps raw model_id → (model_allowlisted ? model_id : "other").
- Maintain per-tier allowlist in config (owned by Applied ML + SRE).

Operationally
- Review allowlist monthly; add/remove based on traffic and product priorities.

3) Separate “SLO computation metrics” vs “product analytics metrics”
If a team wants fine-grained segmentation (SDK version, user agent, etc.), that belongs in analytics (logs/events) not SLO metrics.

4) Sampling for debug metrics
Debug metrics must be sampled at a fixed rate with the rate included in metric help text / dashboards.

5) Retention
- Gold: long retention (quarter+), used for backtesting and budgets.
- Silver: medium (30–60 days) to support investigations and weekly reviews.
- Debug: <= 7 days.


Practical examples

Example 1: Hosted / chat streaming
We can answer:
- “Hosted chat streaming success rate by region” (Gold)
- “Hosted chat streaming disconnect rate by route + model_family” (Silver)
- “What fraction of disconnects are client_abort vs server_disconnect?” (Debug sampled)

Example 2: Dedicated / pinned model
We can answer:
- “Dedicated embeddings p99 latency by region” (Gold)
- “Dedicated embeddings p99 latency by route + model (if allowlisted) else other” (Silver)
- “Is a pool not ready?” (Dedicated readiness gauge by pool)

We explicitly cannot answer via metrics:
- “Per-customer (org_id) p99 by model by route” (too expensive and privacy-sensitive). That goes to restricted logs/analytics or separate customer reporting pipeline.


Privacy + data isolation note (Dedicated)

Even though Dedicated is isolated compute, our metrics platform is shared.

Rules
- No org/customer identifiers on shared Prometheus SLI metrics.
- For customer-specific views, use:
  - Restricted metrics views with pre-aggregated series (e.g., by pool_id) and strict ACLs, OR
  - Offline reporting/exports.

This aligns with the “no data leaks via labels” requirement and keeps cardinality bounded.


Query cost guidance (for dashboards)

We need to make it easy for folks to write queries that don’t accidentally scan the world.

Dashboard rules of thumb
- Always filter by tier and region first.
- Prefer model_family over model.
- Prefer route_group (if we add it) over route for broad views.
- Avoid ad-hoc regex match on route/model; use exact matches.

We should encode these rules into the default Console dashboard templates.


Implementation plan (concrete)

1) Add a shared “slo_labels” helper library
Owners: Telemetry platform + gateway
- Functions:
  - tier_from_context(ctx)
  - endpoint_family_from_route(route_id)
  - canonical_route_id(req)
  - model_bucket(model_id, tier) → allowlisted model or "other"
- This prevents each service from inventing its own label values.

2) Instrumentation updates
- Gateway (Amara): enforce route_id + tier propagation; remove any raw_path usage.
- Routing (Mina/Ravi): adopt model bucketing; ensure region is correct.
- Runtime: emit latency_mode properly (ttft vs e2e); do not add model labels to Gold.

3) Active-series dashboards + alerts
Owners: Logan/Caleb
- Add dashboards per cluster/region:
  - active series by metric name
  - top label sets by series count
  - growth over time
- Add a weekly digest in #eng-observability.

4) CI checks
Owners: Nadia + Thomas
- Lint rules:
  - Prohibit disallowed labels on Gold/Silver metric families
  - Require required labels
  - Require route and model use the canonical helper
- Phase 1 warn-only; Phase 2 block.

5) Migration strategy
We must avoid breaking existing dashboards/alerts.
- Week 0–2: emit new metrics in parallel (new names with _silver suffix where needed)
- Week 2–4: migrate dashboards and SLO queries to new metrics
- Week 4+: deprecate old metrics; remove after 30 days


Open questions / decisions needed

1) Do we need “service” as a label on SLI metrics?
- Pro: easier to query across gateway/routing/runtime.
- Con: adds a small multiplier and encourages “one metric to rule them all.”
Proposal: For Gold, NO (SLOs are per product surface, not per microservice). For Silver, YES only on internal-only dashboard metrics if needed.

2) Streaming latency definitions
We’re currently converging on TTFT as the primary streaming latency SLI. Should we keep e2e stream duration as Silver only?
Proposal: Gold: TTFT only for streaming. Silver: both TTFT and e2e. Debug/logs: disconnect_reason + partial token counts.

3) model label set size
We need to align on initial allowlist sizes.
Proposal: Hosted allowlist N=25 (global), Dedicated allowlist N=25 (global) + “other”. Review monthly.

4) Dedicated pool_id sensitivity
Pool IDs can be considered sensitive. We can hash or use a stable internal ID.
Proposal: pool_id = stable internal numeric ID, not customer name. Access to readiness dashboards restricted to Dedicated oncall + SRE.


Appendix: What will break if we don’t do this

If we ship tier/model/route labels everywhere without guardrails:
- We will almost certainly exceed telemetry budgets during Phase 1 when dashboards expand.
- We will have to roll back labels quickly, at the same time we’re trying to stabilize burn-rate alerting.
- We will be forced to reduce retention or sampling in ad-hoc ways that make SLO backtesting unreliable.

This proposal is meant to prevent that by setting a clear default: “Gold metrics stay small; richer breakdowns live in Silver/Debug with explicit controls.”


Next steps

- Thomas: incorporate feedback from SRE + Console teams by 2026-02-14.
- Logan/Caleb: create active-series dashboards and propose CI linting approach by 2026-02-18.
- Amara + routing/runtime leads: validate feasibility of canonical route + model bucketing by 2026-02-21.
- Aisha/Sergio: confirm label sets align with tiered SLO tables and planned dashboards/alerts by 2026-02-21.

If approved, we should link this doc from the SLO spec as “Observability constraints + labeling standard.”
